{{short description|Mathematical logic}}

In [[mathematical logic]], an '''elementary theory''' is a [[Theory (mathematical logic)|theory]] that involves axioms using only [[finitary]] [[first-order logic]], without reference to [[set theory]] or using any axioms that have [[consistency strength]] equal to set theory.

Saying that a theory is elementary is a weaker condition than saying it is [[algebraic theory|algebraic]].

==Examples==
{{expand section|reason = It would be nice to have some examples of elementary theories which are not algebraic.|date=January 2021}}

Examples of elementary theories include:
* The theory of [[group (mathematics)|groups]]
** The theory of [[finite group]]s
** The theory of [[abelian group]]s
* The theory of [[field (mathematics)|fields]]
** The theory of [[finite fields]]
** The theory of [[real closed field]]s
* [[Tarski's axioms|Axiomization of Euclidean geometry]]
